snippet.title: The Road to Druaga [ザ・ロード・トゥ・ドルアーガ] Game Sample - PC/Doujin
snippet.description:
The gameplay starts about one minute in, was testing different configurations.

"The Road to Druaga" is a cool Doujin fusion of "Dragon Buster" and "The Tower of Druaga" (both influential Namco Arcade games of the mid 80s), developed by Onoda Production which was finished in 2022. The game involves our hero, Gilgamesh, traveling across many maze-like stages to find and rescue the fair maiden, Ki, from the clutches of the evil Druaga. Most items and features from the Tower of Druaga have been converted over and adapted for use in this game, creating a fresh alternative to Dragon Buster while also offering fundamental differences from ToD (namely, the mostly fixed screen and squishy protagonist).The best part? It's free.

The game involves the player travelling a map of different locales which house various secrets that will make your trip easier. Earlier builds of the game didn't have it, but the current version has a hint system on by default which shows which areas house which items to make the game easier for newcomers. Each area is maze-like in structure with many chambers that require you to defeat stronger minions than the free-roaming ones before you can proceed. These minions almost always impart an item that will aid you in your quest, but if it's a piece of equipment, you will want to track down the balancing scales lest you be cursed; Cursed gear always impart some negative side effect (but, interestingly enough, have different abilities from blessed gear, making it worthwhile for those who want a challenge). A key must be found in each area as well before you can progress to the next area.

Gil starts out fairly weak but becomes quite formidable as you get additional gears with different attributes as well as swords to execute combos and rings to defend against will o wisps. Enemies have basic tactics that gradually evolve the further you get into the game and there are also a variety of bosses to defeat with different strategies. Graphically, the game looks slightly more polished than the original Dragon Buster (which means it looks much better than the original Tower of Druaga) and the music seems to be slightly remixed versions of the original ToD at a higher sample rate. For fans of old-school quests, it's a jolly good time.

This is a video of the game in action. You can get it at:

https://druaga.onoda-pro.com/download

Enjoy.
